30418.subject: Chemistry
30418.text: The cycloalkene ( X ) on bromination consumes one mole of bromine per mole of ( X ) and gives the product ( Y ) in which C : Br ratio is 3:1. The percentage of bromine in the product ( Y ) is _ _ _ _ %. (Nearest integer) (Given : molar mass in g mol ⁻¹ H : 1, C : 12, O : 16, Br : 80 )
30418.sol: A cycloalkene (X) undergoes bromination with 1 mole of Br₂, consuming 2 moles of Br atoms (addition to the double bond). The product (Y) has C:Br ratio of 3:1. With 2 Br atoms present, the number of C atoms is 2 × 3 = 6. Therefore, product Y has composition C₆H₁₂Br₂ with molar mass = 6(12) + 12(1) + 2(80) = 72 + 12 + 160 = 244 g/mol. Percentage of Br = (2 × 80 / 244) × 100 = (160 / 244) × 100 = 65.57%, which rounds to 66% (nearest integer).

Given N = 9.6 10²³ atoms, we compute the number of tetrahedral voids as 2 (9.6 10²³) = 19.2 10²³ . Expressed in standard scientific notation, this is 1.92 10²⁴ , which corresponds to option C .

58877.subject: Chemistry
58877.text: In ionic solid, anions are arranged in ccp array and cations occupy 1 / 3 tetrahedral voids. What is the formula of ionic compound? [Consider A = cation ; B = anion]
58877.sol: In a cubic close-packed (ccp) array of anions (B), the number of atoms per unit cell is 4. The number of tetrahedral voids is twice this number, so there are 2 4 = 8 tetrahedral voids. Cations (A) occupy 1 3 of these voids, giving 1 3 8 = 8 3 A ions per unit cell. The ratio of A to B ions is 8 3 : 4 , which simplifies to 2 : 3 by multiplying both sides by 3 and then dividing by 4. The formula of the compound is therefore A ₂ B ₃ , corresponding to option C .

71353.text: Female gametes in a plant have genotypes TR, Tr, tR and tr with respect to height (T/t) and flower colour. (R/r). What will be the phenotype of this plant?
71353.sol: The gametes produced by the plant are TR, Tr, tR, and tr. Since the gametes contain both dominant and recessive alleles for both traits (T and t for height, R and r for flower colour), the parent plant must possess all these alleles. This indicates that the plant is heterozygous for both genes. Thus, the genotype of the plant is TtRr. The phenotype corresponding to the genotype TtRr is heterozygous tall and heterozygous red. Answer: Heterozygous tall; Heterozygous Red (TtRr).

119428.sol: Esters and anhydrides are considered derivatives of carboxylic acids, as mentioned in the paragraph.

119692.subject: Chemistry
119692.text: In nucleophilic substitution reactions, nucleophiles are:
119692.sol: Nucleophiles are electron-rich species that attack electron-deficient parts of a molecule.

120235.subject: Chemistry
120235.text: Who conceived the idea of searching for chemicals that would adversely affect invading bacteria but not the host?
120235.sol: Paul Ehrlich, a German bacteriologist, conceived the idea of searching for such chemicals.

120384.subject: Chemistry
120384.text: How are antibiotics described if they kill or inhibit a wide range of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria?
120384.sol: Antibiotics that kill or inhibit a wide range of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria are described as broad spectrum antibiotics.

120420.subject: Chemistry
120420.text: Why is the use of aspartame limited to cold foods and drinks?
options: Aspartame is unstable at high temperatures and breaks down.
Aspartame is too sweet for hot foods.
Aspartame loses its flavor when heated.
120420.sol: Correct Option is : (A) Aspartame is unstable at high temperatures and breaks down.

120916.subject: Chemistry
120916.text: Give the reason why the two strands in DNA are not identical but are complementary
options: The two strands in DNA are not identical because they are synthesized from different sets of genes.
The two strands in DNA molecule are held together by hydrogen bonding, which is according to a specific rule(A
The two strands in DNA are complementary because they have the same sequences of nucleotides.
The two strands in DNA are not identical because they have different chemical structures.
120916.sol: Correct Option is : (B) The two strands in DNA molecule are held together by hydrogen bonding, which is according to a specific rule(Adenine is bound thymine and guanine to cytosine).Due to this base pairing principle, the sequence of bases in one strand automatically fixes the sequence of bases in the other stand. Thus, the two strands are not identical but are complimentary.

121167.subject: Botany
121167.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Lion ( Panthera lio), leopard (P. pardus) and tiger (P. tigris) with several common features, are all species of the genus Panthera. Reason: The genus Panthera differs from another genus Felis which includes cats.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
121167.sol: Lion ( Panthera lio), leopard (P. pardus) and tiger (P. tigris) with several common features, are all species of the genus Panthera. The genus Panthera differs from another genus Felis which includes cats.

121541.subject: Botany
121541.text: Members of Phycomycetes are found in i. Aquatic habitats ii. On decaying wood iii. Moist and damp places iv. As obligate parasites on plants Choose from the following options
121541.sol: Members of Phycomycetes are found in Aquatic habitats, On decaying wood, Moist and damp places and occur as obligate parasites on plants.

121655.subject: Botany
121655.text: Water bloom is generally caused by
121655.sol: Water blooms are formed by the growth of some microscopic or semi-microscopic algae, such as, Anabaena, Arthrospira, Nodularia, Nostoc, etc. Water blooms are harmful, as they are responsible for the depletion of oxygen in water bodies.

122168.subject: Botany
122168.sol: Chlorella, commonly known as space alga is a protein rich alga, containing about 50 % protein, 20 % lipids, 20 % carbohydrates and a little percentage of vitamin- B ₂, ~B ₁₂, C , H , K etc.

122174.subject: Botany
122174.text: Plants growing on sand and gravel are called
122174.sol: Psammophytes grow in sand and gravel, eremophytes grow in desert and gravel, psilophytes grow in savanna and oxylophytes grow on acidic soil.

122328.subject: Botany
122328.text: How many statements are correct about this organism? A- They have two pairs of gills which are covered by an operculum on each side. B- Sexes are separate C- Fertilisation is usually internal. D- They are mostly oviparous and development is direct. E-Betta is also called angelfish.
122328.sol: B,D and E are correct They have four pairs of gills which are covered by an operculum on each side. Fertilization is usually external. They are mostly oviparous and development is direct.

122406.subject: Botany
122406.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Fasciola are diploblastic animals 2. Platyhelminthes undergo external fertilisation 3. Members of Platyhelminthes contain hookers and suckers 4. Taenia are coelomates
122406.sol: Members of Platyhelminthes contain hookers and suckers in their parasitic forms that help them to absorb nutrients from the host directly through their body surface.

122549.subject: Botany
122549.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In Columba , the long bones are hollow with air cavities and air sacs are connected to the lungs. Reason (R): Pneumatic bones reduce body weight and air sacs supplement respiration to meet the high energy demands of flight. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer fr
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
122549.sol: Columba (Pigeon) belongs to the class Aves. Assertion (A) is correct: Birds possess a fully ossified endoskeleton where the long bones are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic bones). Additionally, they have air sacs connected to their lungs. Reason (R) is also correct and explains the Assertion: These anatomical features are crucial flight adaptations. Pneumatic bones make the body lighter, while air sacs supplement respiration to provide the high amount of oxygen required for the energy-intensive process of flight

122875.subject: Botany
122875.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The shape and colour of corolla vary greatly in plants. Reason: Corolla may be tubular, bell-shaped, funnel shaped or wheel-shaped.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
122875.sol: The shape and colour of corolla vary greatly in plants. Corolla may be tubular, bell-shaped, funnel shaped or wheel-shaped.

122982.subject: Botany
122982.text: While studying the floral morphology of angiosperms, a student compares the families Fabaceae, Solanaceae, and Liliaceae. Which of the following gynoecium characteristics is exclusively found in family Liliaceae among the three?
options: Bicarpellary, syncarpous ovary with swollen placenta
Tricarpellary, syncarpous ovary with axile placentation
Monocarpellary, superior ovary with marginal placentation
Tricarpellary, apocarpous ovary with parietal placentation
122982.sol: According to NCERT, the gynoecium of family Liliaceae is tricarpellary, syncarpous with a superior ovary and axile placentation. Family Fabaceae has a monocarpellary, superior ovary with marginal placentation. Family Solanaceae has a bicarpellary, syncarpous, superior ovary with axile placentation and a characteristic swollen placenta. Therefore, the tricarpellary, syncarpous condition is specific to Liliaceae among the three families. The option stating apocarpous and parietal placentation is incorrect for Liliace

123220.subject: Botany
123220.text: What is the function of the waxy material suberin found in the endodermal cells?
options: To act as a barrier for the uptake of minerals
123220.sol: The outermost layer is epiblema. Many of the cells of epiblema protrude in the form of unicellular root hairs. The cortex consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells with intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. The tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of casparian strips. Next to endod

123729.subject: Botany
123729.text: When do the centromeres divide during mitosis?
123729.sol: Mitosis is also divided into four stages namely prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. Chromosome condensation occurs during prophase. Simultaneously, the centrioles move to the opposite poles. The nuclear envelope and the nucleolus disappear and the spindle fibres start appearing. Metaphase is marked by the alignment of chromosomes at the equatorial plate During anaphase, the centromeres divide and the chromatids start moving towards the two opposite poles. Once the chromatids reach the two poles, the chromo

123782.subject: Botany
123782.text: During Diplotene, the paired chromosomes form an X-shaped structure called ___.
123782.sol: During Diplotene, the paired chromosomes form an X-shaped structure called Chiasmata

124226.subject: Botany
124226.text: Types of Vacuoles Functions A. Contractile vacuole 1. Stores excess water B. Food vacuole 2. Digests engulfed food particles C. Storage vacuole 3. Stores nutrients, waste, and maintains turgor pressure D. Central vacuole 4. Stores substances in plant cells
124226.sol: The contractile vacuole stores excess water, the food vacuole digests engulfed food particles, the storage vacuole stores nutrients and waste, and the central vacuole maintains turgor pressure in plant cells.

124593.subject: Botany
124593.text: What is one of the primary roles of abscisic acid (ABA) in plants?
124593.sol: ABA stimulates the closure of stomata in the epidermis and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses. Therefore, it is also called the stress hormone ABA plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy. By inducing dormancy, ABA helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth.

124595.subject: Botany
124595.text: Which plant physiological process is stimulated by ABA?
124595.sol: ABA stimulates the closure of stomata in the epidermis and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses. Therefore, it is also called the stress hormone. ABA plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy. By inducing dormancy, ABA helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth.

124856.subject: Botany
124856.text: A cell is equally permeable to sucrose solution and NaCl solution. First the cell is put in 0.6 M sucrose solution there is no change in size but when put in 0.6 M NaCl solution the size will
124856.sol: 0.6 M NaCl solution is hypertonic to 0.6 M sucrose solution because there are more solutes per unit volume in NaCl solution as compared to sucrose solution. Hence, when the cell is placed in 0.6 M NaCl solution after being placed in 0.6 M sucrose solution water will move out of it and its size will decrease on account of exosmosis.

125166.subject: Botany
125166.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the reactions of glycolysis. List-I List-II A. Glucose ( ) Glucose-6-phosphate I. ATP is utilized B. 3-phosphoglyceraldehyde ( ) 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate II. NADH + H (^+ ) is produced C. 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate ( ) 3-phosphoglyceric acid III. ATP is synthesized D. 2-phosphoglycerate ( ) Phosphoenolpyruvate IV. H (₂ )O is removed Choose the correct answer from the options given belo
125166.sol: In the glycolysis pathway: - The conversion of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate is a phosphorylation step where ATP is utilized (A-I). - The conversion of 3-phosphoglyceraldehyde (PGAL) to 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (BPGA) is an oxidation step where NAD (^+ ) is reduced to NADH + H (^+ ) (B-II). - The conversion of 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate to 3-phosphoglyceric acid (PGA) is an energy-yielding step where ATP is synthesized from ADP (C-III). - The conversion of 2-phosphoglycerate to phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) involves the r

125608.subject: Botany
125608.text: In Sugarcane, what is the first stable product of CO ₂ fixation and in which specific cells is it formed?
options: Oxaloacetic acid in bundle sheath cells
125608.sol: Sugarcane is a C ₄ plant exhibiting Kranz anatomy. In C ₄ plants, the initial CO ₂ fixation occurs in the mesophyll cells where Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) acts as the primary acceptor in the presence of PEP carboxylase to form the 4-carbon compound Oxaloacetic acid (OAA). Thus, OAA is the first stable product and it is formed in the mesophyll cells. The Calvin cycle (where PGA is formed) occurs later in the bundle sheath cells. Students often confuse the location of initial fixation or mistake Sugarcane for a C ₃ p

125686.subject: Botany
125686.text: C ₄ plants have better productivity because
options: C ₄ plants absorb more light
C ₄ plants absorb more CO ₂
125686.sol: Presence of photorespiration is considered as a wasteful and energy consuming process in crop plants which ultimately leads to reduction in final yield of crops. It is estimated that during C ₃ photosynthesis, upto 50 % of the CO ₂ fixed may have to pass through photorespiratory process, thereby resulting in considerable decrease in photosynthetic productivity. In C ₃ plants, there is some loss of photosynthetic activity on account of photorespiration which is absent in C ₄ plants and hence they have better product

125740.subject: Botany
125740.text: Which of the following cell organelles is associated with photorespiration?
125740.sol: Photorespiration ( C ₂ -cycle) is a special type of respiration shown by many green plants ( C ₃ -plants) when they are exposed to light. It is a light dependent process during, which O ₂ is used and CO ₂ is released. The process of photorespiration takes place only in chlorophyllous tissues of plants. Therefore, the main site for photorespiration is chloroplast. But mitochondria and peroxysomes are also required to complete the process.

126387.subject: Botany
126387.text: Why is vivipary an undesirable character for annual crop plants?
options: It reduces the vigour of plant
The seeds cannot be stored under normal conditions for the next season
It adversely affects the fertility of the plant
126387.sol: Vivipary is the condition when seeds germinate on the plant. It is an undesirable character for annual crop plants because germinated seeds cannot be stored under normal conditions for the next season.

127009.subject: Botany
127009.text: DDT residues are rapidly passed through food chain causing biomagnification because DDT is
127009.sol: Many of pesticides, such as DDT, aldrin and dieldrin are accumulated in the environment. They are fat soluble and generally non-biodegradable. They get incorporated into the food chain and ultimately deposited in the fatty tissues of animals and humans. In the food chain, because of their build up, they get magnified in the higher trophic levels called biological magnification. The phenomenon of biological magnification is also reported of certain other pollutants such as, heavy metals, eg, Mercury, copper and radi

127049.subject: Botany
127049.text: Which of the following is not an invasive species?
127049.sol: Non-native or alien species are often introduced inadvertently for their economic and other uses. They often become invasive and drive away the local species. These species are considered to be second major cause of extinction of species (the first being habitat destruction). Lantana camara has replaced many species in forests of Central India. Parthenium hystero-phorus has pushed out several herbs and shrubs from open places in the plains. Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) was introduced in Indian waters to re

127347.subject: Botany
127347.text: What is the significance of the slope of regression in a species - area relationship?
options: to show it to the world
to bring the statistical data about the number of species
127347.sol: The slope is very helpful in finding the species - area relationship.

127667.subject: Botany
127667.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Forest, grassland and desert are some examples of terrestrial ecosystems. Reason: Crop fields and an aquarium may be considered as natural ecosystems.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
127667.sol: Forest, grassland and desert are some examples of terrestrial ecosystems while pond, lake, wetland, river and estuary are some examples of aquatic ecosystems. Crop fields and an aquarium may also be considered as man-made ecosystems.

128470.subject: Zoology
128470.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine Reason: The hormones of adrenal cortex is known as catecholamines
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128470.sol: The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine. The hormones of adrenal medulla is known as catecholamines

129241.subject: Zoology
129241.text: What divides the cerebrum into two halves?
129241.sol: A deep cleft divides the cerebrum longitudinally into two halves, which are called the left and right cerebral hemispheres. The cerebral cortex contains motor areas, sensory areas, and large regions that are neither clearly sensory nor motor in function. These regions, called the association areas, are responsible for complex functions such as intersensory associations, memory and communication. The layer of cells which covers the cerebral hemisphere is called the cerebral cortex. The cerebral cortex contains motor

129465.subject: Zoology
129465.text: What are protonephridia primarily concerned with?
129465.sol: A survey of animal kingdom presents a variety of excretory structures. In most of the invertebrates, these structures are simple tubular forms whereas vertebrates have complex tubular organs called kidneys. Some of these structures are mentioned here. Protonephridia or flame cells are the excretory structures in Platyhelminthes (Flatworms, e.g., Planaria), rotifers, some annelids and the cephalochordate – Amphioxus. Protonephridia are primarily concerned with ionic and fluid volume regulation , i.e., osmoregulation

129721.subject: Zoology
129721.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The glomerular filtrate becomes increasingly hypertonic as it moves down the descending limb of the loop of Henle. Reason (R): The descending limb of the loop of Henle is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
129721.sol: Assertion (A) is true because as the filtrate flows down the descending limb of the loop of Henle, water moves out of the tubule into the hyperosmotic medullary interstitium, concentrating the filtrate and making it hypertonic. Reason (R) is true because the descending limb is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes. This selective permeability is exactly what causes the water efflux and the resulting concentration of the filtrate. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct expla

129760.subject: Zoology
129760.text: The excretory material of bony fish is
129760.sol: The excretory and osmoregulatory organs of fishes are the gills and kidney. Excretion in bony fishes is ureotelic (ie, they excrete urea) but some fresh water bony fishes are ammonotelic (ie, excrete ammonia).

129778.subject: Zoology
129778.text: How is the process of respiration performed in organisms?
129778.sol: The process of respiration in organisms is performed through breathing, commonly known as respiration. As you have read earlier, oxygen (O2) is utilised by the organisms to indirectly break down simple molecules like glucose, amino acids, fatty acids, etc., to derive energy to perform various activities. Carbon dioxide (CO2) which is harmful is also released during the above catabolic reactions. It is, therefore, evident that O2 has to be continuously provided to the cells and CO2 produced by the cells have to be r

129988.subject: Zoology
129988.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Lower invertebrates like coelenterate exchange O2 with CO2 through gills 2. Gills are used by most earthworms for respiration 3. Earthworms use their moist cuticle and insects have a network of tubes to transport atmospheric air within the body 4. Among vertebrates, fishes use gills whereas amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals respire through lungs
129988.sol: Lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, flatworms, etc., exchange O2 with CO2 by simple diffusion over their entire body surface. Earthworms use their moist cuticle and insects have a network of tubes (tracheal tubes) to transport atmospheric air within the body. Special vascularised structures called gills (branchial respiration) are used by most of the aquatic arthropods and molluscs whereas vascularised bags called lungs (pulmonary respiration) are used by the terrestrial forms for the exchange of gases

130957.subject: Zoology
130957.text: Label a, b, and c from the diagrammatic view of the male reproductive system (part of the testis is open to show inner details).
options: a - Rete testis, b - Vasa efferentia, c - Epididymis
a - Vasa efferentia, b - Epididymis, c - Bulbourethral gland
a - Epididymis, b - Rete testis, c - Vasa efferentia

131003.subject: Zoology
131003.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Each testis has about one to three compartments called testicular lobules. Reason: Each lobule contains about 250 highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
131003.sol: Each testis has about 250 compartments called testicular lobules. Each lobule contains about one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced

131752.subject: Zoology
131752.text: A form of genetic variation wherein different nucleotide sequences can be present at different sites in a molecule of DNA is called ____
131752.sol: A form of genetic variation wherein different nucleotide sequences can be present at different sites in a molecule of DNA is called polymorphism.

131833.subject: Zoology
131833.text: In the experiments conducted by Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty to determine the biochemical nature of the 'transforming principle', the addition of which of the following enzymes inhibited the transformation of R strain bacteria to S strain?
131833.sol: Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty purified biochemicals (proteins, DNA, RNA, etc.) from the heat-killed S cells to see which ones could transform live R cells into S cells. They discovered that protein-digesting enzymes (proteases) and RNA-digesting enzymes (RNases) did not affect transformation, so the transforming substance was not a protein or RNA. Digestion with DNase did inhibit transformation, suggesting that the DNA caused the transformation. This proved that DNA is the hereditary material. Answer: DNase

131900.subject: Zoology
131900.text: In living systems, DNA is preferred for the storage of genetic information, whereas RNA is preferred for the transmission of genetic information. Which of the following pairs of properties best justifies this functional division?
options: DNA can directly code for the synthesis of proteins, whereas RNA is chemically highly stable and resists mutat
DNA has a higher mutation rate facilitating rapid evolution, whereas RNA acts exclusively as a structural comp
DNA is chemically less reactive and structurally more stable, whereas RNA can directly code for the synthesis
DNA is single-stranded making it compact for storage, whereas RNA contains thymine making it suitable for tran
131900.sol: According to NCERT, DNA is chemically less reactive and structurally more stable compared to RNA, which makes it a better genetic material for the storage of genetic information. On the other hand, RNA is preferred for the transmission of genetic information because it can directly code for the synthesis of proteins. DNA is dependent on RNA for protein synthesis. The other options contain incorrect biological facts: DNA does not directly code for proteins, RNA is not highly stable, DNA does not have a higher mutati

132020.subject: Zoology
132020.sol: Non-genetic RNA is found in all eukaryotic and prokaryotic organisms. It is of three types i.e., (i) Ribosomal RNA ( r -RNA) (ii) Transfer RNA ( t -RNA) (iii) Messenger RNA (m-RNA)

132056.subject: Zoology
132056.text: What type of plants did Mendel cross to study the inheritance of one gene?
132056.sol: Mendel where he crossed tall and dwarf pea plants to study the inheritance of one gene (Figure 4.2). He collected the seeds produced as a result of this cross and grew them to generate plants of the first hybrid generation. This generation is also called the Filial1 progeny or the F1 . Mendel observed that all the F1 progeny plants were tall, like one of its parents; none were dwarf (Figure 4.3). He made similar observations for the other pairs of traits – he found that the F1 always resembled either one of the par

132798.subject: Zoology
132798.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Biochemical similarities among diverse organisms suggest a common ancestry. Reason: Similarities in proteins and genes performing a given function among different organisms provide clues to shared ancestry.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
132798.sol: Biochemical similarities, such as in proteins and genes, indicate that diverse organisms may share a common ancestry.

132969.subject: Zoology
132969.text: Match List I with List II: Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
132969.sol: The correct answer is option no. (3)

133590.subject: Zoology
133590.text: Assertion : Protooncogenes are present in normal cells. Reason : Protooncogenes may causes malignant tumour in animals, if activated.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.

134408.subject: Zoology
134408.text: What is the definition of biotechnology given by the European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB)?
options: The integration of natural science and organisms
134408.sol: Further, many other processes/techniques are also included under biotechnology. For example, in vitro fertilisation leading to a ‘test-tube’ baby, synthesising a gene and using it, developing a DNA vaccine or correcting a defective gene, are all part of biotechnology. The European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB) has given a definition of biotechnology that encompasses both traditional view and modern molecular biotechnology. The definition given by EFB is as follows: ‘The integration of natural science and organi

134587.subject: Zoology
134587.text: After 30 cycles of PCR, how many times will DNA be amplified?
134587.sol: The enzyme extends the primers using the nucleotides provided in the reaction and the genomic DNA as template. If the process of replication of DNA is repeated many times, the segment of DNA can be amplified to approximately billion times, i.e., 1 billion copies are made. Such repeated amplification is achieved by the use of a thermostable DNA polymerase (isolated from a bacterium, Thermus aquaticus), which remain active during the high temperature induced denaturation of double stranded DNA.

135010.subject: Zoology
135010.text: Recombinant DNA technology involves several steps in which initial step is of isolation of the DNA. Which enzymes are used in the process for the break down of fungal cell, plant cell and bacterial cell respectively?
135010.sol: Processes of recombinant DNA technology involves isolation of DNA of a desired DNA fragment. In order to cut the DNA with restriction enzymes, it needs to be in pure form, free from other macro molecules. The DNA is enclosed within the membranes, we have to break the cell open to release DNA along with other macromolecules such as RNA, proteins, polysaccharides and also lipids. This can be achieved by treating the bacterial cells/plant or animal tissue with enzymes such as lysozyme (bacteria), cellulase (plant cell

135026.subject: Zoology
135026.sol: - Plant transformation mediated by the soil pathogen, Agrobacterium tumefaciens has become the most used method for plant transformation. - It naturally infects the wound sites in dicots causing the crown gall disease. It is capable to transfer T-DNA of the Tumour inducing (Ti) plasmid into the nucleus of infected cells. - It will then integrate into the host genome and is transcribed, causing the crown gall disease. - Thus, the correct answer is option C.

135042.subject: Zoology
135042.text: Which of the following levels of biological organization is not explored?
135042.sol: Ecology is a subject which studies the interactions among organisms and between the organism and its physical (abiotic) environment. Ecology is basically concerned with four levels of biological organization – organisms, populations, communities and biomes. All the cormorants in a wetland, rats in an abandoned dwelling, teakwood trees in a forest tract, bacteria in a culture plate and lotus plants in a pond, are some examples of a population. In earlier chapters you have learnt that although an individual organism

135466.subject: Zoology
135466.text: Which one of the following is a matching pair of certain organism(s) and the kind of association?
options: Algae and fungi in lichens - mutualism
Cuscuta (dodder) growing in other flowering plants - epiphytism.
135466.sol: The association between fungi and algae in lichen is regarded as the true mutual relationship, in which both the partners are benefitted. In lichen, fungus lives on the algae which manufactures food by virtue of the chlorophyll present in its cells, while the algae enjoys the protection afforded by the fungal envelope, to live in very dry conditions.

6a104ff88b46719ce7976cde.subject: Physics
6a104ff88b46719ce7976cde.text: A long, straight horizontal wire carries a steady current I from left to right as shown in the figure. Two circular conducting loops, P and Q, are placed in the same plane as the wire. Loop P is located above the wire and is moving vertically upwards with velocity v . Loop Q is located below the wire and is also moving vertically upwards with velocity v . According to Lenz's law, what will be the direction of the ind
options: Anticlockwise in both P and Q
Anticlockwise in P and Clockwise in Q

Species Genus Order Family Class Phylum Kingdom
Species Genus Family Order Class Phylum Kingdom
6a1bb6be107bf677676d9f6f.sol: The taxonomic hierarchy is the arrangement of various taxonomic categories in a definite order. is perpendicular to the acceleration for a single instant only
is always perpendicular to the acceleration
is perpendicular to the acceleration for two distinct instants
304549.sol: In projectile motion, the acceleration is constant and acts vertically downwards, a = -g j . The velocity of the projectile at any instant t is given by v = u i + (u - gt) j . For velocity to be perpendicular to acceleration, their dot product must be zero. v a = 0 -g(u - gt) = 0 t = u g This time corresponds to the highest point of the trajectory. Since there is only one such instant during the motion, the velocity is perpendicular to the acceleration for a single instant only.

6a7a1ff87fac6178dbd942df.text: The enthalpy change when a sample of solid benzene ( C ₆ H ₆ ) completely melts at its melting point is 39.6 kJ . If the molar enthalpy of fusion of benzene is 9.9 kJ mol ⁻¹ , the mass of the benzene sample melted is ________ g .
6a7a1ff87fac6178dbd942df.sol: Molar mass of benzene ( C ₆ H ₆ ) = 6 12 + 6 1 = 78 g mol ⁻¹ Number of moles of benzene melted, n = Total enthalpy change Molar enthalpy of fusion n = 39.6 kJ 9.9 kJ mol ⁻¹ = 4 moles Mass of benzene = n Molar mass = 4 mol 78 g mol ⁻¹ = 312 g Answer: 312

6a7a1ff80ae730e42e34a90d.sol: Photochemical bromination is highly regioselective, favoring the formation of the most stable free radical intermediate. 6a7a1ff85b0f5e6c7f061fbe.text: Phenol reacts with Br ₂ in CS ₂ at 273 K to give a major product P. P reacts with aqueous NaOH followed by CH ₃ I to give Q. Q is heated with concentrated HI to give an aromatic product R and an aliphatic product S. Identify the structures of P, Q, and R.
options: P is 2,4,6-tribromophenol; Q is 2,4,6-tribromoanisole; R is 2,4,6-tribromophenol
P is 4-bromophenol; Q is 4-bromoanisole; R is 4-bromophenol
P is 4-bromophenol; Q is 4-bromoanisole; R is 1-bromo-4-iodobenzene
P is 4-bromophenol; Q is 4-bromoanisole; R is 4-iodophenol
6a7a1ff85b0f5e6c7f061fbe.sol: Phenol reacts with Br ₂ in a non-polar solvent ( CS ₂ ) at low temperature to undergo monohalogenation. The major product P is 4-bromophenol. 4-bromophenol reacts with aqueous NaOH to form sodium 4-bromophenoxide, which then undergoes Williamson ether synthesis with CH ₃ I to form 4-bromoanisole (Q).
